passage:
At fifteen, Indu felt her cheeks flame every time the teacher called on her. She was sure the whole class was staring, so she looked at the floor and mumbled. One day Tenzin, her music teacher, paused the lesson and said, "Look at the window and tell me one thing you can see." Indu breathed out slowly, looked at a crow on the ledge, and answered in a steadier voice. Nobody had turned to stare; most of them were looking at their own notebooks.

At twenty-one, on the morning of her viva, Indu's hands shook and her palms were damp. She had rehearsed her answers with her friend Baljeet the night before. Now she pressed her feet into the floor, counted five breaths and told herself, "My body is getting ready." When the first question came, she began speaking, and the shaking eased. She had decided that if it ever grew into panic that stayed, she would go to the college counsellor.

qa.q: What did Indu see when Tenzin asked her to look at the window?
qa.a: Indu saw a crow on the ledge.

qa.q: What did Indu learn about handling her body's signals between fifteen and twenty-one?
qa.a: At fifteen she used a slow breath and looked outward, discovering that few people had noticed her blush; at twenty-one she added preparation, feet on the floor and counted breaths, and read the shaking as her body getting ready.

qa.q: What was Indu feeling when her cheeks flamed at fifteen?
qa.a: Indu was anxious and self-conscious, sure that everyone was staring at her.

qa.q: Why did Indu rehearse with Baljeet before the viva?
qa.a: Preparation calms nerves, and answering aloud to a friend meant she had practised her responses before the shaky, high-stakes moment.

grounding: Visible reactions with several causes: a teenager's blushing and a young adult's shaky hands, each softened with breathing, focusing outward and reframing nerves.
